subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Tribeca Retail (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@tribecaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Tribeca Retail (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the call today, Sam — great to meet the team and see the scope for the in-store checkout assistant POC. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off:

High-level POC goals
- Validate that Redwood inference can serve the receipts/checkout assistant at production-like latency and cost while keeping accuracy within acceptable bounds.
- Establish configuration that meets Tribeca’s latency and throughput SLOs and a quantifiable quality baseline for product acceptance.

Proposed success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 256-token requests (customer-facing assistant responses)
- Throughput: sustained 50 QPS for inference endpoint with autoscale burst to 150 QPS for peak events
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0006 (target to be refined with real token distribution)
- Quality: >= 92% accuracy on the checkout intent classification tasks and <= 5% critical-failure rate on a reserved eval set (we’ll define what counts as critical)

Evaluation plan & ownership
- Tribeca provides a representative eval dataset (redacted receipts + labeled intents) — Sam to share by next Tue (we discussed a CSV manifest).
- Redwood will run controlled A/B evaluation on dedicated capacity and provide latency/throughput/cost traces and quality metrics. (Dev/Marissa owning the Redwood side).

Timeline & next steps
1) Sam to share dataset and success criteria clarifications by Tue 01/12.
2) Redwood to provision a dedicated POC environment and share onboarding doc by Thu 01/14.
3) Kickoff run and baseline evaluation week of 01/18; 2-week trial.

Attachments: POC scope draft attached (Tribeca_POC_scope_v1.pdf).

If this looks good I’ll follow up with the detailed mutual action plan and calendar invites.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference for production-grade LLMs
From: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@tribecaretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Tribeca Retail (post-call recap)

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the clear list. Agree with most of this; a few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms is what we want for the assistant replies — that aligns with our in-store UX target.
- Throughput: the baseline 50 QPS is fine; need to confirm peak concurrency during promo windows (I’ll try to get load estimates by EOD Wed).
- Cost: target is important but secondary for the POC; we need to show we can hit latency at reasonable cost.
- Quality: we’ll provide an eval set with accept/critical labels. For acceptance we want >= 90% on intent accuracy and < 3% critical failures for launch readiness; 92% is preferred.

I’m attaching the dataset manifest and a short note on labeling conventions (tribeca_eval_dataset_manifest.csv).

Timeline: we can share the full dataset by Wed 01/13. Kickoff week of 01/18 works for us.

Thanks — Sam
Head of Product — Conversational Experience
Tribeca Retail

[Attachment: tribeca_eval_dataset_manifest.csv]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@tribecaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Tribeca Retail (post-call recap)

Appreciate the quick reply and the manifest, Sam — that’s perfect. Two small adjustments from our side based on internal ops: 

- Cost token target: we’ll track both raw cost/token and end-to-end per-response cost. Proposal: report cost/token + estimated $/session using your average token distribution; set an exploratory target of <= $0.0006/token for the POC and then refine.
- Throughput validation: Redwood will run synthetic load tests and a second run using replayed production traces (if you can provide sample traffic logs, redacted). This will help us validate autoscale behavior and cold-starts.

Concrete evaluation metrics we’ll deliver at the end of the trial:
1) Latency report: p50/p90/p95/p99 for both cold and steady-state; distribution plot and 95th percentile per-route.
2) Throughput: sustained QPS achieved, fail/retry rates, and autoscale timeline for burst scenarios.
3) Cost: token-level cost and estimated $/session for your dataset.
4) Quality: confusion matrix on intents, precision/recall, and a small hand-eval sample for critical-failure verification.

Ownership summary:
- Tribeca: provide eval dataset, sample traffic traces (optional), define critical failures.
- Redwood: provision environment, run evals, deliver report and recommendations (Marissa/Dev lead the execution).

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Marissa will schedule the POC kickoff + link to the onboarding doc.
- I’ll circulate the mutual action plan with dates and owners after kickoff is scheduled.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@tribecaretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Tribeca Retail (post-call recap)

Sam — I’ve provisioned a dedicated POC pool for Tribeca and started a stub environment. Dev and I will own the run and the report.

Quick ask: can you confirm the expected average token length per assistant response (ballpark is fine) and whether we should include multimodal attachments (images of receipts) in the eval set? That will affect memory and KV-cache sizing.

I’ll put a calendar invite for the kickoff (01/18 10am PT) — please accept if that works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sam Nguyen <sam.nguyen@tribecaretail.com>

Marissa/Jordan — confirmed. Average assistant response is ~120 tokens; we will include redacted receipt images for ~10% of cases (we’ll surface links not raw files). I accepted the 01/18 10am PT kickoff.

We’ll send the dataset and sample traces by EOD. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Sam
